subject.title: feat(gateway): wire read coding tool into HTTP /tools/invoke (narrow)

question: Should OpenClaw core expose the built-in host-filesystem `read` tool through Gateway direct invocation when `gateway.tools.allow` includes `read`, `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead` is true, and the caller is owner/admin?
rationale: Automated review can validate the gates and compatibility behavior, but it cannot decide whether authenticated direct host-file access belongs in the core threat model.

options.title: Accept narrow read boundary
options.body: Approve the read-only capability with the proposed triple gate, audit warning, workspace-confinement guidance, and plugin-name compatibility.

options.title: Keep host reads agent-only
options.body: Reject the new direct-invoke capability and preserve the current Gateway host-data boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow read boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the read-only capability with the proposed triple gate, audit warning, workspace-confinement guidance, and plugin-name compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: They tightened and merged the shared direct-invoke contract and were explicitly requested to review this boundary.
